newsitem.title: INDIA: TENNIS-TILLSTROM OVERCOMES EXHAUSTION TO BAG TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-TILLSTROM OVERCOMES EXHAUSTION TO BAG TITLE.

text.p: Sweden's Mikael Tillstrom won his first ATP Tour singles title on Sunday with a 6-4 4-6 7-5 victory in an eventful Indian Open final against Alex Radulescu of Germany.

Sixth seed Tillstrom, 25, received icepack treatment on court during the third set to overcome exhaustation but finally wore down the fifth-seeded Radulescu's resistance in a two-and-a half-hour duel.
"It's a dream come true," said Tillstrom, the world's 61st-ranked player who has had to wait five years for his maiden singles title after winning his first ATP Tour doubles crown in 1992.
The match hinged on a controversial line call in the 10th game of the third set which saw Radulescu, who served 11 aces to Tillstrom's five, serving for the match at 5-4.
Chair umpire Romono Grillotti of Italy ruled in Tillstrom's favour to give the Swede a crucial break point, prompting Radulescu to hurl his racket to the ground in disgust.
"I'm sorry I behaved like that," he said. "I don't know what happened to me. I was completely shattered the moment the point was overruled by chair umpire and that affected my game.
"It was impossible to continue after such a decision... but in my heart I have won this title."
Tillstrom, who showed remarkable reach in retrieving several Radulescu drop shots, had earlier consistently attacked his opponent's backhand and hit down-the-line winners on both sides of the court.
He looked in control after taking the first set with a service break in the ninth game and led 4-1 in the second set, before the Romanian-born Radulescu charged back.
